text:
Marathon Petroleum jumped 5.4% today on a sharp spike in crude oil prices—Brent crude surged more than 4% after reports that the U.S. is deploying a third aircraft-carrier strike group to the Middle East, an escalation tied to tensions involving Iran. For a refiner like Marathon, higher crude prices can initially boost profits if the company can pass costs along to customers through fuel prices, and the geopolitical risk premium being priced into oil today signals tighter global supply conditions that favor refiners.

The move also reflects a broader energy market tightening: U.S. refineries are running at 92.5% capacity—near maximum utilization—while crude exports through the Strait of Hormuz have recovered to prewar levels, though that recovery depends on continued U.S. military protection of tanker traffic in the Persian Gulf. This combination of tight refining capacity and supply-chain vulnerability means Marathon stands to benefit from the price strength, at least in the near term.
